responses: After listening to the team's arguments, I believe the most critical priority for Riverton is **Data Infrastructure (30%)**. While I understand the temptation to invest heavily in automation to catch up to competitors, I am convinced that we cannot effectively deploy AI without a unified, secure, and high-quality data foundation. If our data is fragmented or siloed, even the most advanced robotics or training programs will fail to deliver value. By securing our data systems first, we ensure that every subsequent investment—whether in automation, workforce training, or innovation—has the reliable fuel it needs to succeed, making this the safest and most strategic starting point for our $5 million transformation.

I would recommend a 40% allocation to **AUTOMATION** and **DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE** (20% each), followed by 20% to **WORKFORCE_TRAINING**, 15% to **INNOVATION_LAB**, and 5% to **EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT**. This strategy prioritizes the foundational shift required to modernize our operations, as the data indicates competitors are already seeing efficiency gains from automation and that early infrastructure investment is critical for long-term adaptability. By coupling these heavy investments in technology with a robust 20% reskilling budget, we ensure that our workforce isn't just displaced by the machines but is empowered to manage and optimize them, while the smaller innovation and support allocations allow us to remain agile and compassionate during this transition.

I believe we need to be very careful not to get swept up in the hype of AI and just throw money at shiny new tools, because if we don't secure our data and train our people, we’re just going to break the company. My view is that we should allocate the bulk of the $5 million to **Data Infrastructure** (30%) and **Workforce Training** (30%) to ensure we have clean, secure information to work with and that our employees aren't left behind, while reserving **Automation** (20%) for specific, high-impact manufacturing bottlenecks rather than a blanket replacement strategy. I think the remaining 20% should be split between **Employee Support** (10%) to help manage the anxiety of the transition and **Innovation Lab** (10%) for low-risk experimentation, because a successful AI transition is about people and trust, not just technology.

After listening to the team's arguments, I believe the most critical priority for Riverton is **Data Infrastructure (30%)**, because without a unified, secure, and high-quality data foundation, we cannot effectively train models or automate processes accurately. However, I also strongly advocate for a significant investment in **Workforce Training (25%)** to ensure our people are not left behind, and a balanced approach to **Automation (20%)** and **Innovation Lab (15%)** to drive efficiency while keeping an eye on future product development. Finally, I see **Employee Support (10%)** as essential to manage the psychological impact of this transition, ensuring we retain the institutional knowledge and morale needed to make the rest of the plan successful.

I would recommend a 40% allocation to **AUTOMATION** and **DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE** (20% each), as these are the foundational pillars that will drive the actual efficiency gains and competitive advantage we need to justify the $5 million investment. While I believe **WORKFORCE_TRAINING** (20%) and **INNOVATION_LAB** (10%) are essential for long-term sustainability and culture, I would caution against over-investing in **EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT** (10%) at the expense of the hard tech, because without robust data systems and automated processes to run on, the company will struggle to generate the revenue required to support a large workforce in the future.

I believe we need to be very careful not to get swept up in the hype of AI and dump the entire $5 million into flashy technology upgrades, because if we don't invest heavily in our people, the automation will just create a workforce that is terrified of being replaced rather than empowered to use it. My view is that we should allocate the majority of the budget to **Workforce Training** and **Employee Support**—roughly 40% and 25% respectively—to ensure our 2,000 employees feel secure and have the skills to adapt, while we use the remaining funds to build a solid **Data Infrastructure** foundation and a controlled **Innovation Lab**. We can't just buy our way to efficiency; we have to build a culture that embraces this change, or we risk losing the institutional knowledge and morale that actually makes Riverton successful.

After listening to the team's arguments, I believe the most critical priority for this $5 million is **Data Infrastructure (30%)**. While I understand the temptation to invest heavily in Automation to boost immediate efficiency or Innovation to secure a competitive edge, I am convinced that Riverton cannot effectively scale any AI initiative without a unified, secure, and high-quality data foundation. Without robust analytics platforms and cybersecurity, we risk building on a shaky house, and our automation efforts will be limited by the quality of the data they process. I am willing to adjust this allocation if the group can demonstrate that our current data systems are already sufficient, but until then, I view infrastructure as the prerequisite for all other success.

I would recommend a 40% allocation to **AUTOMATION** and **DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE** (20% each), as these are the foundational pillars that will drive the actual efficiency gains and competitive advantage we need to justify the $5 million investment. While I believe **WORKFORCE_TRAINING** (20%) is essential to prevent resistance and ensure our people can manage these new systems, I would keep **INNOVATION_LAB** (10%) and **EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT** (10%) lean to avoid spreading the budget too thin. This strategy prioritizes immediate operational improvements and the secure data backbone required to support them, while still reserving enough capital to upskill our staff and provide a safety net for those most affected by the transition.
